## Summary

`catalyst env shell` named its writable home volume from the image digest alone, so every repository using the same image mounted the same `/home/catalyst`. Code run in repository A could leave a `.bash_profile` that ran when repository B's shell opened, with B's checkout and declared secrets available. The volume name now also carries a hash of the checkout path, so each repository folder gets its own home.

## Ticket requirements

- **Scope the volume per repository.** Met. `homeVolumeFor(image, root)` (`src/env/shell-plan.ts:42-46`) returns `catalyst-env-home-<12 hex of image digest>-<24 hex of sha256(root)>`. Its only caller passes `input.root` (`src/env/shell-plan.ts:84`), the host path bind-mounted at `/workspace`. That path cannot be changed from inside the container; I did not key on the origin URL or git common dir, because the checkout's own files decide those. `shell` and `--check` in one folder share a name, so toolchains and history still persist per repository, and a new image still starts fresh.
- **Acceptance: a test that fails on a1126ea9 and passes with the fix.** Met. Two tests compare the volume mount of two roots on one image:
  - `test/env-shell-plan.test.ts:39`, on the argv builder (`shellRunArgs`).
  - `test/env-shell.test.ts:468`, through `main`, with the same origin name and git common dir for both checkouts; it also checks that `--check` reuses the shell's volume.
  
  Validation ran the first test against `a1126ea9` (fetched through `refs/pull/407/head`) and it failed with both repositories getting the identical volume word. Against current main's `src/` with this branch's tests, 6 tests fail, including both new ones. At this head they pass.

## Changes Made

- `src/env/shell-plan.ts`: `homeVolumeFor` takes the checkout root and returns a fixed-length name (55 characters); header comment updated. `ShellRunInput` is unchanged.
- `test/env-shell-plan.test.ts`: pinned volume name updated in the existing assertions; new tests for two repositories getting different volumes, one repository keeping its own across shell, non-terminal and `--check` modes and a different git common dir, and a name-format test for odd roots (spaces, non-ASCII, 400-character and Windows-style paths).
- `test/env-shell.test.ts`: the through-`main` test above.
- `thoughts/shared/`: research, plan and validation documents for CTC-6155.

Old shared volumes (`catalyst-env-home-<12 hex>`) stay on disk unused. Moving a repository to a new path, or reusing a path for a different repository, changes or keeps its volume accordingly. The plan accepts both. The git common dir mount is a separate path that the plan leaves to a follow-up ticket.

## Changelog Entry

Fixed: `catalyst env shell` keeps a separate home volume for each repository folder, so a shell in one repository can no longer plant startup files that run in another.
